---
title: "Write the Brief"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
**Prerequisites:** a companion from the Kennel. **Objective:** write prompts that make output checkable, and manage the context window so the agent stays on task.
**Time:** about 15 minutes. <span class="ao-badge">Last verified (docs, not run): Claude Code v2.1.323 and OpenCode docs on 2026-11-13 (sources in `research/forest-and-reef.md`).</span>
:::

The first branch of the skill tree is the **brief**: what you tell the agent. A vague brief invites a plausible guess. A good brief names the file and the symptom, says what "done" looks like, and gives the agent a **check it can run**.

| Vague | Specific |
|---|---|
| "Fix the GC script." | "`gc.py` reports 20.0 for `seq2` in `tiny.fasta` but `awk` gives 60.0. Find why and fix it. Done when both agree." |
| "Make it faster." | "Profile `align.py` on `small.fa`, name the slowest function, and propose a change. Do not edit files yet." |

Two habits make the rest of this safer:

- **Plan first.** In Claude Code, plan mode (`Shift+Tab`, or `/plan`) lets the agent read and propose a plan with no source edits until you approve. Read the plan the way you would read a methods section.
- **Ask for evidence.** "Show the command and its output" turns a claim into something you can look at.

## Context is a budget

Everything in the conversation competes for the model's attention. Old, unrelated material can crowd out what matters.

::: {.panel-tabset group="companion"}

## Claude Code

`/context` shows what is filling the window. `/compact` summarises the conversation (you can say what to keep). `/clear` starts fresh, which is right when you switch to an unrelated task. Claude Code also compacts automatically near the limit.

## OpenCode + Ollama

`/compact` (alias `/summarize`) summarises the session and `/new` (alias `/clear`) starts a new one. The docs show no `/context` equivalent in the TUI. A small local model has a short window, so start fresh more often.

:::
